class_guess: Layered Bell counter: budget phases with a x4/3, mod-3-branching layer law (cryptid-like)
summary: Phases convert one budget block per 4-trip cycle; each new layer is ~4/3 the last and n mod 3 picks the next phase.
mechanism: Trip and phase level: three short trips cross the unary counter 1001^c, the fourth converts one budget block; the budget sum is conserved and c grows by 2 per cycle (R1-R3 validated 60/60, 40/40, 40/40).
Epoch level: at a phase end the counter (about 8n cells) becomes a layer of (4n+r)/3 blocks, and n mod 3 picks the next phase (0: H6 shift phase, 1: R1 phase at once, 2: re-eat an older layer).
To 1e11: layers 5803, 9996, 13333, 17774; the old 9996 layer is re-eaten at 4.8e10..8e10 and rebuilt; no halt (halting needs B> 111, never written).

rules.from: phase 6 with budget n = g+h (real 1.29e10 configuration, h varied)
rules.to: new layer of (4n+r)/3 blocks; n = 0 mod 3: H6->H6 shift phase; 1 mod 3: R1 phase at once; 2 mod 3: re-eats the older 5803 layer

template.diff: no table within 5 transitions; architecture comparison only
template.note: Our W5-3 kill (machines/<W5-3>/ .v, read). R1-R3 are linear walk lemmas like W5-3's Wk/W2Q. W5-3 closes its eats with a binary counter and one size bound; here the phase ends feed a x4/3 layer law with a mod-3 branch, which no template covers.

strategy: Parked under the cryptid protocol. If funded: build an exact phase-level accelerator from R1-R3 plus measured phase-end maps, run it far past 1e11, and census the residue branches for a closed set of phase shapes.
risks: The layer law n -> (4n+r)/3 with a mod-3 choice of successor phase is Collatz-like (Hydra-style x3/2 relatives); a closed invariant may not exist.
Phase ends were measured on 6 instances from one real configuration only; other phase types may have other offsets.
Phases reach back into older layers (9996 re-eaten at 4.8e10), so the state is a stack of layers, not one counter.
